note: Local FastAPI GPU monitor with no login of any kind. The product calls no model API and has no AI tools. The only model use is a local llama.cpp README translator in CI (scripts/translate.py), which is build tooling. No secrets, env files or Supabase. SQLite queries are parameterized and subprocess calls use argument lists. POST /api/processes/terminate is registered twice (lines 649 and 968); FastAPI uses the first, so the second handler and the code after the returns at lines 698-715 never run. Without CuPy or PyTorch the benchmark runs in a disclosed 'passive' mode that does no work. README marks macOS Apple Silicon monitoring as done, but the GPU collector is NVIDIA-only (NVML or nvidia-smi). Images, locale READMEs and scripts/*.txt word lists were skipped. No file was blocked.

labels.what: Web server binds to 0.0.0.0, so every unauthenticated endpoint (kill process, shutdown, self-update, elevated restart, process and port lists) is open to the whole network. The code default is 127.0.0.1
web.host is 0.0.0.0 in config.yaml but 127.0.0.1 in DEFAULT_CONFIG, so the same setting has two different values and the shipped file wins

POST /api/processes/terminate kills any PID on the host, including system processes. There is no login; the only gate is a server-wide is_admin flag, so every client that reaches the port has full kill rights
is_admin is true when the process runs as root or was simply started with --admin. It is a server-wide mode, not a user role, and it unlocks process killing for every visitor

POST /api/vram_caps has no admin or login check. The dashboard disables the cap slider and input for non-admins, so the gate exists only in client code. On an admin server, a new cap immediately kills watched PIDs (lines 753-868)
DELETE /api/vram_caps clears all caps and releases VRAM reserves with no auth check
POST /api/shutdown stops the monitor for anyone who can reach the port, with no auth check
POST /api/update/install lets any client make the server download the latest release and overwrite its own code files, with no auth check

POST /api/restart_elevated has no auth and takes client-supplied args. The inplace mode re-execs the app with those args (for example --admin, which turns on the kill endpoints without real elevation). Windows only
GET /api/processes, /api/ports (line 621) and /api/launch_args (line 1131) expose process names, owners, the first command-line args and open ports to any client, with no auth

POST /api/benchmark/start has no auth and no bounds on duration, matrix_size, num_particles or backend_multiplier. temp_limit=0 turns off the thermal stop (metrics_sampler.py line 122), so any client can run an unbounded GPU stress test
The /ws/simulation WebSocket has no auth, takes a client-chosen particle count with no limit and runs for a fixed 3600 seconds
Auto-kill also terminates any other process on the GPU with the same name as a watched PID, even if it is not on the watchlist

13 PIDs from the author's machine are committed and loaded as the kill watchlist at startup. On another machine they belong to unrelated processes, which the admin-mode cap watcher terminates when GPU 0 is over its cap
A committed VRAM cap of 16% on GPU 0 is loaded at startup. The watcher then raises a desktop 'VRAM Exceeded' toast every 5 seconds whenever GPU 0 is above 16%, and kills watched PIDs in admin mode
cap_mb is cast to int with no range check, so 0 or a negative cap is accepted and every watched process on that GPU counts as over the cap. Only the UI rejects values of 0 or less
Process name and username go into innerHTML unescaped. A local user can name a process with HTML and run script in the dashboard, which can call the kill, shutdown and update endpoints
Port table puts process_name into innerHTML unescaped, the same stored XSS path as the process table
Alert messages go into innerHTML unescaped. Server alerts embed process names (server.py line 307)
Chart.js loads from a CDN with no version pin, and all four CDN scripts lack integrity hashes, on a page that can kill processes

Self-update downloads the release zip and copies its files over the current working directory with no checksum or signature check. perform_update (lines 171-186) installs even when the release is not newer
macOS notification builds an AppleScript string with an f-string and no escaping of title or message
CPU 95%, memory 95% and disk 90% alert thresholds are hardcoded. config.yaml sets cpu_usage_warn, memory_usage_warn and disk_usage_warn to 90, but the code never reads them
cluster.name is set twice with two different values ('My GPU Cluster' and 'Prototype Cluster Monitor'); YAML keeps the last one
history_retention_hours: 168 is never applied. cleanup_old_data is never called, and every GET /api/status writes new rows, so metrics.db grows forever
Package version is '1.2.0' here but '2.1.0' in monitor/__version__.py, and update.py falls back to '1.2.0' (line 19)
Update source is hardcoded to the DataBoySu/MyGPU GitHub releases API, also duplicated in utils.js line 227
Router defaults differ from BenchmarkConfig: num_particles 100000 here and 30000 in config.py line 16, plus target_gpu_util fixed at 98 (line 45)
Simulation run is hardcoded to 3600 seconds and a 100 ms sample interval
Available history metrics are a fixed list that only covers GPU 0, so other GPUs' history cannot be chosen
Particle-mode TFLOPS is an estimate from a fixed 50 FLOPs per particle step, but it is reported as measured TFLOPS

Quick, Standard and Extended buttons promise 15, 60 and 180 seconds at 4096x4096, but startBenchmark sends only the mode name. The router ignores mode presets and always runs 30 seconds at matrix 2048, then saves the result as the GPU baseline
'VRAM cap saved' shows on any HTTP 200, but the server answers 200 with status 'error' for bad input (same at lines 256-258)
After a fixed 3-second setTimeout the loader turns green and shows 'System Offline', whether or not the shutdown call worked
Check for Updates shows a green success toast with the latest tag only. It never compares it with the running version and does not use the server's /api/update/check
The watchlist checkbox ignores the response. A non-admin server rejects the add with HTTP 200 and an error, but the box stays checked until the next refresh

No Origin check or CSRF token. /api/shutdown, /api/update/install and /api/benchmark/start take no JSON body, so any web page the user visits can send them as simple cross-site POSTs to the local dashboard, even when it binds to 127.0.0.1
